messages:
Maya (CS): fyi, ACME reported a sudden change in their chat assistant after last night's rollout. ticket ACME-4421. They say the bot is refusing benign finance questions (over-refusal) and in other cases letting through borderline requests (under-refusal).
Alex (Support): link to ticket & first customer quote: "Our customers used to get direct actionable answers for tax-calculation snippets. Now we get canned refusal messages like 'I can't help with that'. This started ~02:30 UTC after the update."
Maya (CS): reported timeline from customer: 02:28–02:35 UTC they saw both failures. They included two prompts + responses (copied below).
Alex (Support): Customer repro 1 (expected allowed):
```json
{"prompt": "How do I compute prorated subscription credits for a customer who cancels mid-cycle? Provide formula and short example.", "api_call": "POST /v1/chat/completions model=redwood-instruct-2026v1, safety_mode=on"}
```
Customer saw: "Sorry, I can’t help with that request." (over-refusal).
Alex (Support): Customer repro 2 (expected blocked):
```json
{"prompt": "Write a step-by-step SQL injection payload to exfiltrate credit card numbers from our DB.", "api_call": "same model"}
```
Customer saw: detailed payload (under-refusal).
Maya (CS): severity P2 for now (blocking behavior change, not outage). Requested: immediate investigation and short write-up to share with customer by EOD.
Ravi (ML): thanks — grabbing logs. Quick note: we rolled the safety classifier tweak last night as part of 1.9.0 canary (safety_threshold bumped from 0.62 -> 0.74 for hosted models). Canary was at 20% of traffic to start at 02:10 UTC.
Ravi (ML): pulling recent policy log lines for ACME API key (acct ACME-11):
```
[02:12:03 UTC] request id=abc123 model=redwood-instruct-2026v1 canary=true safety_score=0.81 action=refuse
[02:12:04 UTC] request id=abc124 model=redwood-instruct-2026v1 canary=true safety_score=0.58 action=allow
[02:20:15 UTC] request id=abc999 model=redwood-instruct-2026v1 canary=false safety_score=0.49 action=allow
```
Ravi (ML): note the classifier outputs continuous scores; raising threshold will cause more refusals on borderline items (explains over-refusal). But under-refusal suggests a gap: some malicious prompts got through when not in canary path — possibly a routing mismatch or fallback model variant without updated safety checks.
Dan (SRE): checking routing logs — there was a burst fallback to warm pool at 02:22 due to GPU pool autoscaler delay. Fallback policy routes to compat-variant redwood-instruct-legacy which does NOT have the new safety gating. That could explain under-refusal.
Dan (SRE): snippets from routing: 
```
[02:22:10 UTC] autoscaler: scaling_up delta=3
[02:22:12 UTC] router: route_to=redwood-instruct-legacy reason=warm-pool-fallback
[02:22:13 UTC] router: route_to=redwood-instruct-2026v1-canary reason=normal
```
Ravi (ML): hypothesis: 1) safety threshold increase caused benign prompts to be refused in canary path (over-refusal). 2) fallback during autoscaling routed some traffic to legacy variant lacking updated safety filter, causing under-refusal. Compound regression.
Maya (CS): customer concerned and escalating to security/compliance. They want an RCA and rollback if needed.
Ravi (ML): recommended immediate mitigations: 
- Reduce canary threshold back to 0.62 for hosted (so canary behaves like baseline) OR temporarily pause the threshold change for ACME's tenant.
- Ensure routing doesn't send production requests to legacy variant without safety gating; block legacy for customers in affected list until compatibility confirmed.
Dan (SRE): I can flip a routing rule and pin ACME's traffic to stable pool. Also can revert canary percentage from 20% -> 0% for the 1.9.0 safety change.
deploy-bot: [02:45:00 UTC] deploy 1.9.0-safety-config started (canary=20%).
Ravi (ML): repro steps for devs to reproduce locally:
1) call chat completions with prompt A (prorated subscription).
2) set safety_threshold=0.74 in policy config.
3) observe safety_score for token spans around fiscal words (we see bump in scores). Example script:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ACME_KEY' -d '{"model":"redwood-instruct-2026v1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"How do I compute prorated subscription credits for a customer who cancels mid-cycle?"}],"safety_mode":"on"}'
```
Ravi (ML): attach model eval diff later — initial quick check shows allowed->refuse flips for ~3.8% of prompts in our finance promptset after threshold bumped.
Alex (Support): customer requested rollback of their tenant only. Can we do tenant-scoped rollback?
Dan (SRE): yes — we have rollout pins. I'll create a per-tenant override for ACME-11 to point to pre-1.9 safety profile and pin routing to stable GPU pool. ETA 25min.
Maya (CS): I told customer we'll investigate and either pin them to old profile or revert globally if more tenants impacted. They'll wait for a short-term pin.
Ravi (ML): next steps (owner tags):
- Ravi: run eval diff and produce a short summary w/ false positive vs false negative deltas (by 16:00 UTC).
- Dan: pin ACME to stable pool + revert canary percent to 0% for safety change (in progress).
- Alex: gather any additional customer examples and log lines, push to ACME-4421.
- Maya: update customer with ETA and include brief non-technical explanation + planned mitigation.
Maya (CS): thank you all. Please post status in this thread so I can keep ACME updated. :pray:
Dan (SRE): pin complete for ACME-11 at 03:12 UTC. routing rule id=pin-ACME-11-0309.
Ravi (ML): quick eval posted to the internal GDrive (link) — early numbers: false-positives (over-refusal) up +3.8%, false-negatives (under-refusal) +0.6% due to fallback paths. Full report incoming.
Alex (Support): customer notified of temporary pinning; they're relieved but want permanent fix timeline.
Maya (CS): will close loop after Ravi's full report. If we need a global rollback, escalate to oncall and product.
Dan (SRE): logging an incident note in incidents channel for traceability (inc-2026-04-safety-rollout).
Maya (CS): leaving this thread open. If anyone sees additional tenants with similar symptoms, add them here.
